title.narrative: Emergency Response and Recovery for the 2025 Typhoons and Floods

description.narrative: During 2025, Viet Nam experienced a series of severe and compounding climate-related disasters, including Typhoons Bualoi, Matmo, Fengshen, and Kalmaegi, which triggered widespread flooding, landslides, and extensive damage to housing, infrastructure, livelihoods, and essential services across multiple regions. The cumulative impacts of these successive events disproportionately affected vulnerable populations, particularly in the Central Highlands and Northern mountainous provinces, including Gia Lai, Dak Lak, Da Nang, Cao Bang, Lang Son, Tuyen Quang, Phu Tho, Bac Ninh and Thai Nguyen provinces, where ethnic minority communities, poor and near-poor households, women-headed households, older persons, and persons with disabilities faced heightened risks and limited recovery capacity.In response to these emergencies, the Government of Viet Nam requested continued international support to address urgent humanitarian needs while advancing early recovery and resilience-building efforts, as reflected in the 2025 Joint Response Plan (JRP) and its Addendum. These frameworks underscore the need for integrated, multi-sectoral interventions that bridge immediate relief with medium-term recovery, while reducing future disaster and climate risks.Given UNDP’s longstanding role and comparative advantage in disaster response, early recovery, and resilience building in Viet Nam, timely and coordinated intervention is essential. In close collaboration with national and provincial authorities, United Nations agencies, and development partners—including support from the Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) and the Australian Embassy and other donors/partners—UNDP is implementing this Initiation Plan to guide emergency response and recovery interventions during 2026–2027.This Initiation Plan is aligned with UNDP’s post-disaster recovery strategy and encompasses actions across the early recovery continuum.
